# HRange

> A native numeric slider with a visible value and optional unit.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This reference describes repository source; package.json version: 0.2.0. Match it to the source/release you are using.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HRange` from `@samishal1998/hearth-ui`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-range>`.
- Individual constructor: `HearthRangeElement` from `@samishal1998/hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Controls.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HRange.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- The model and emitted payload are numbers; FormData serializes the value as a string.
- The native range input owns bounds, stepping, and keyboard behavior. The visible output reflects its actual stepped value.
- Use valid finite min/max/step values, with a positive step.

## Public API

label, name, unit, hint: string · modelValue, value, min, max, step: number · disabled: boolean

A `?` marks optional source props. A prop with a default may be omitted even when the source type is required. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    modelValue?: number;
    value?: number;
    label: string;
    name?: string;
    min?: number;
    max?: number;
    step?: number;
    unit?: string;
    hint?: string;
    disabled?: boolean;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{ value: 0, min: 0, max: 100, step: 1, unit: "" }
```

### Events

update:modelValue(number), change(number)

```ts
type Emits = {
    "update:modelValue": [
        value: number
    ];
    change: [
        value: number
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose arguments as `event.detail`, an array. Listen directly on the element. Native DOM events such as `click` keep their normal payloads.

### Slots

None

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Custom elements do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, label, value, control

Use `hearth-range::part(part-name)` for an exposed part, or inherited `--h-*` tokens for system-level styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';
import { HRange } from '@samishal1998/hearth-ui';
import '@samishal1998/hearth-ui/styles.css';
const minutes = ref(15);
</script>

<template>
  <HRange v-model="minutes" label="Refresh interval" name="interval" :min="5" :max="60" :step="5" unit=" min" />
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point (use a `form` instead of `div` when demonstrating field submission):

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

The following is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a stylesheet link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Set array/object properties before connection when they should become reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@samishal1998/hearth-ui/elements';
import '@samishal1998/hearth-ui/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-range');
Object.assign(element, {
  "label": "Refresh interval",
  "name": "interval",
  "value": 15,
  "min": 5,
  "max": 60,
  "step": 5,
  "unit": " min"
});
element.addEventListener('change', event => {
  const [value] = event.detail;
  // Update your application state using value.
});
mount.append(element);
```
